punchline: Low-ranking baboons carried higher stress hormones even with no danger present.
thirty_sec: Sapolsky spent thirty summers among wild baboons, because their stress, like ours, is social. He tracked who dominated whom and measured the hormones in their blood. Baboons at the bottom of the hierarchy carried higher cortisol even at rest, with no predator in sight. Yet what mattered was not rank alone but how it was lived; stability, allies and an outlet for frustration changed everything.
question: In your own circle, is there someone you trust and can vent your tension to?
key_contrast: Not rank itself but how you live that rank shapes your health.
